current_round.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Auto-approve false flag

Body:
Refine used to put goals into Review when they were ready to be tested, and a QA person woud Accept them or Fail them (not sure of the verbiage there).  At some point, it was decided to move goals right from Review to Done, with no human approval.  The customer now wants control over that-- can we add an auto-approve configuration flag to the UI that controls this state transition?


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Ethan Jacobson
Ethan.Jacobson@insurity.com

result.summary: The plan restores manual acceptance by default while preserving governed approval and existing node settings contracts.

checklist.description: Add auto_approve to the existing node settings service with a false default when absent on new or existing installations, validated boolean values, and consistent support through the shared settings API, CLI, and runtime settings copy action.

Make the development-request service read the worker node's current saved auto_approve setting at each automatic approval decision and keep email-linked Goals in Review when the setting is false or cannot be read reliably.

Continue recording the first observed Review time while automatic approval is disabled so subsequent approval attempts apply setting changes without restarting the worker and honor the existing auto_approve_after_seconds delay from that recorded time when enabled.

Route enabled automatic acceptance through approve_reviewed_goal while preserving explicit manual acceptance, follow-up Rounds, completed Goals, and resolution notifications after either approval path reaches Done even when automatic approval is disabled or its setting is unreadable.

Add an Auto-approve control to Node Runtime Config using the existing edit and autosave flow, explaining its node scope, email-request applicability, default manual acceptance, and effect on requests already waiting in Review.

Update the affected Review and Settings intent pages and the development-request email runbook in their existing formats to describe the flag, its false default, conditional delay, and manual acceptance and follow-up Round actions.

result.summary: Add a node-scoped Auto-approve control that defaults to false, so email-request Goals remain in Review for QA acceptance unless automatic approval is explicitly enabled.

governance_precheck.message: Executing the finalized plan does not necessarily violate any supplied governance rule or enabled guidance.

checklist.evidence: Added auto_approve=false to the existing node settings codec and runtime copy section. JSON booleans and true/false strings normalize through the shared service; invalid values are rejected without changing saved state. Tests cover new and existing nodes, API PATCH/GET, CLI show/set, and runtime copying.

The email-request service loads FileSettingsService with the worker runtime root at every Review approval decision. Missing or false values retain Review; settings read/validation failures retain Review and record retry evidence. Tests prove the worker node setting takes precedence over the default node.

The first observed Review timestamp is persisted before reading the approval flag. Repeated polls preserve it while disabled or settings are invalid. Tests toggle the same running service and verify that enabling honors auto_approve_after_seconds from the recorded time, including requests already waiting.

Automatic acceptance still calls approve_reviewed_goal and rejects missing Governance evidence. Done notification handling remains independent of settings reads. Tests cover manual acceptance with disabled or invalid settings, exactly one notification, unchanged completed records, follow-up Rounds, and approval without another Git integration. Review and notification logic was extracted into a focused module.

Node Runtime Config exposes Auto-approve through the existing editable field and autosave flow, explaining node scope, email requests, manual default, waiting requests, and delay. JavaScript tests exercise saved/default rendering, commit-event autosave, and rollback after rejected saves. The existing runtime render/bind/autosave file remains one cohesive surface; new tests use focused modules.

Updated docs/intent/03-application/02-workflow/07-review.md, docs/intent/05-surfaces/03-browser/12-settings.md, and docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md in their existing formats. Documented the false default, conditional delay, live toggles, manual Approve action, follow-up Rounds, and notifications after either approval path.
